audit.whatIsWrong: Three chart rows disagreed with the packet and with the page's own why text: row 0 said Neeko while whys[0] says 'Level 1 is a skill lane', row 1 said Skill while whys[1] says it tilts to Yasuo, and row 4 said Neeko against a packet value of Skill. diff also read EVEN while diffRating is 7.5/10 and report[14] calls it tricky.
audit.why: The packet chart is [Skill, Yasuo, Yasuo, Yasuo, Skill, Yasuo, Yasuo] and the mirror (neeko__yasuo) was already realigned to those packet values as an atomic group, so the two pages would otherwise render different answers. The prose on this page already agreed with the packet — only the side tokens were wrong.
audit.corrected: Proposed rows 0, 1 and 4 as paired flips (phases[N].side + win[N]) with matching ratings, and moved diff from EVEN to TRICKY so it agrees with the 7.5/10, the amber tone and report[14].

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4] and whys[5] were off by one row: whys[4] (the Level 6 row) described level 5, and whys[5] (the First item row) described level 6.
audit.why: Row 4 is labelled Level 6 and row 5 is First item. Every stage label after 4-5 was therefore describing the previous spike, which shifts the player's whole recall and all-in plan by one power window.
audit.corrected: Rewrote whys[4] as the Level 6 read (hidden Pop Blossom) and whys[5] as the first-item read (crit kills her on the Tangle-Barbs gap).
sources: phases[N].label values in the full layer

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] and wants.foe[1] name 'Pop Away (P clone)'. That ability does not exist. Neeko's passive is Inherent Glamour (a disguise) and the clone is Shapesplitter (W). No cooldown numbers appeared anywhere.
audit.why: This is the same class of error as 'Ares of Blaze' for Pyroclasm — a fabricated name in the field the player is told to track. Shapesplitter is 16/15/14/13/12s; Tangle-Barbs is 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s and grows larger, faster and longer-rooting after passing through a champion, which is the detail that makes dodging it near a minion wave different from dodging it in open ground; Blooming Burst is a 9s blockable projectile; Pop Blossom is 120s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Replaced the fabricated name in spikes[1].text and wants.foe[1], and wrote the real cooldowns into breakdown.cooldowns, winCon, report[1].t and report[9].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entire page rests on 'Wind Wall blocks Tangle-Barbs (E)' and I could not confirm it from the data available.
audit.why: Blooming Burst (Q) carries the projectile flag, so the wall certainly eats her poke. Tangle-Barbs carries hardCC but no projectile flag, while Riot's own description says she 'slings a tangle that damages and roots everything it passes through' — which reads as a travelling skillshot. Flag and description conflict, and the mirror audit hit the same wall and left it open.
audit.corrected: No edit made in either direction. I did not remove the claim (deleting a probably-true interaction is as damaging as inventing one) and I did not reinforce it. Recorded as unverified and as a question.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page calls Neeko 'him' and 'his' throughout.
audit.why: Neeko is female and the content layer already uses 'her', so the two layers read as different champions.
audit.corrected: Fixed the highest-visibility instances: tldr, winCon, report[0].t, report[1].t, report[9].t, dosFull[2].t and dontsFull[0].d.

notes: UNRESOLVED and load-bearing: this page tells the player in five places that Wind Wall blocks Tangle-Barbs (E). The kit gives E a hardCC flag but no projectile flag, while Riot's text says the tangle 'passes through' enemies. I left every one of those lines untouched — asserting it or deleting it are both risks I will not take without confirmation. Blooming Burst (Q) is flagged projectile, so the Wind-Wall-eats-her-poke half is safe. 'Pop Away (P clone)' was a fabricated ability name and is gone. Also note the remaining he/his references to Neeko in tradeGood, tradeBad, breakdown.feeding, report[3], report[11] and report[12] — those strings are duplicated across breakdown and report, so a scripted pronoun pass is safer than hand edits.
